validity.recommendation: update Diameter to 48 (single line, current-per-record design) rather than 42; keep Length as recorded
validity.researcher_notes: Pipeline exists and is correctly classified/attributed at the system level; this is a value-currency finding, not an existence doubt. As originally proposed (FERC pre-filing request filed 2019-04-17, approved 2019-04-30; Federal Register NOI 2019-08-07), Delta Express was TWO PARALLEL 42-inch pipelines in a single ~283-mile right-of-way (confirmed by the 2019-08-07 Federal Register NOI, the 2019-04 NaturalGasIntel article on the initial FERC letter which gives 287 mi/42-in/17 parishes LA+2 counties MS, and The Advocate's 2019 article: '283-mile pipeline...42-inch wide', 14 parishes Richland-to-Plaquemines, cost $8.5B). GEM's recorded Diameter=42/LengthKnown=281 mi matches THIS original design. But Venture Global filed a Supplemental NOI (Federal Register, 2020-01-28) stating the project was revised: 'Delta LNG no longer proposes to construct' three of four compressor stations and 'now proposes to construct: A single 48-inch-diameter pipeline along the previously proposed route' (~285 mi, same 14 LA parishes, Alto + new Melville compressor stations) -- this is the LAST KNOWN design change before the 2025-06-10 withdrawal; no later filing reverting to dual 42-inch lines was found. A secondary aggregator (nsenergybusiness.com/GlobalData) independently corroborates the single 48-inch design and the Alto/Melville compressor stations, though it renders length as '~485 km' (~301 mi), which looks like a unit-conversion error against its own 14-parish/route description and does not match any primary filing -- not used. Note: offshore-technology.com's withdrawal writeup separately lists a GlobalData report referencing 'Delta Express Line I Pipeline' and 'Delta Express Line II Pipeline', which appears to be a stale two-line label left over from the pre-2020 dual-pipe concept; no separate GEM PID exists for a 'Line II' in this roster, so this is NOT staged as a duplicate -- flagging it here for awareness only, in case GEM's own wiki page or another tracker later needs reconciling against it. LENGTH: kept as recorded (281 mi) -- within rounding of all three vintages found (280 mi Southerly 2020, 283 mi Federal Register 2019, ~285 mi Federal Register 2020); no material discrepancy.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: 'Shelved' (not 'cancelled') is the right call and the sheet's own LastUpdated (2025-09-16) already reflects the newest evidence: Venture Global formally withdrew the Delta LNG/Delta Express pre-filing application from FERC on 2025-06-10/11 (OGJ, offshore-technology.com, both citing the same FERC letter -- two independent write-ups of one origin document), stating it would focus on the faster Plaquemines Expansion instead. Upstream Online separately reports the company intends to retain the Delta land for a possible future revival if market conditions improve, which is exactly the 'shelved, not dead' signal that distinguishes this from a confirmed cancellation. As of 2026-09 the withdrawal is ~15 months old -- well under the 4-year shelved->cancelled dormancy threshold -- so no staleness rule applies; checked Venture Global's most recent SEC 10-Q (period ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026) and found zero mentions of 'Delta' anywhere in the filing, consistent with a dormant/shelved project that has not been revived or formally killed. No search found any subsequent FERC filing, sponsor statement, or press report changing this status since the June 2025 withdrawal.

summary: P2737 Delta Express (Venture Global): real, existing project correctly recorded as shelved (confirmed, June 2025 FERC pre-filing withdrawal, 2 independent sources; not yet at the 4y cancellation threshold). Two caveats staged: Diameter should be 48in not 42 (project was redesigned from two 42-in lines to one 48-in line per a 2020 FERC supplemental notice, before the 2025 withdrawal), and Operator's legal name should read 'Venture Global Delta Express, LLC' not 'Delta Express Pipeline LLC'. No existence, duplicate, or classification concerns. UNRESOLVED: Pressure, ConstructionYear (never reached), FuelSource, SegmentCost (only a combined terminal+pipeline $8.5B figure exists). EIA follow-up pass: closed Capacity as REFS_ADDED at 2000 MMcf/d (medium tier, single EIA source -- FERC filings state no capacity figure, Venture Global's site no longer references the shelved project, and the prior pass's uncited '2.0+ Bcf/d' lead turns out to likely describe the unrelated, similarly-named DeLa Express pipeline, not this one); SegmentCost stays UNRESOLVED (EIA's cost field is blank for this project in all 24 releases).
